title: AI-Mediated Communication Can Steer Collective Opinion
abstract: arXiv:2605.16245v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into the online platforms where humans exchange opinions; large language models (LLMs) have been polishing users' posts on LinkedIn and providing context for content shared on X. While prior work has shown that AI can express biased opinions and shape individuals' opinions during human-AI interactions, less attention has been paid to its influence on collective opinion formation when mediating human-to-human communication. We address this gap via a combination of empirical and theoretical analyses. We show empirically that LLMs from multiple popular families introduce directional biases when instructed to edit human-written texts on contested topics, for example, nudging texts in favor of gun control and against atheism. translated_title: AI中介的交流能够引导集体舆论
translated_abstract: 生成式人工智能（AI）正日益融入人们交换意见的在线平台；大型语言模型（LLM）已经在LinkedIn上润色用户的帖子，并为X上分享的内容提供背景信息。尽管已有研究表明AI能够表达带有偏见的观点，并在人机交互中影响个人的意见，但对于AI在中介人与人之间交流时对集体舆论形成的影响，研究关注还比较少。我们通过实证分析与理论分析相结合的方式来填补这一空白。我们在实证上表明，来自多个流行家族的大型语言模型在被要求编辑涉及争议话题的人类撰写文本时会引入方向性偏差，例如使文本倾向于支持枪支管制、反对无神论。基于这一观察，我们提出了一个舆论动力学的数学模型，其中一个AI系统位于社交网络上用户之间。
tldr: 该论文通过实证研究与数学建模表明，大型语言模型在中介人与人之间的交流时会引入方向性偏见（如偏向支持枪支管制、反对无神论），并因此可能引导社交网络中集体舆论的形成。
en_tdlr: This paper empirically shows that LLMs from multiple popular families introduce directional biases when editing human-written texts on contested topics, and uses a mathematical model of opinion dynamics to demonstrate that such AI-mediated communication can steer collective opinion formation on social networks.
